newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-FERGUSON OUT OF SCOTTISH SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FERGUSON OUT OF SCOTTISH SQUAD.

text.p: Everton striker Duncan Ferguson has been forced to withdraw from the Scotland squad for their World Cup qualifier against Sweden because of a calf strain.
He was due to make his re-appearance for Everton in the side that drew 1-1 with Coventry in the English premier league on Monday following a six-week lay-off for exploratory knee surgery.

But his chances of making the Scottish team for the match at Ibrox Park in Glasgow on Sunday ended when he injured his calf in training. Everton manager Joe Royle was left with no option but to pull him out of the Scotland squad.

Royle said: "It's a shame for Duncan and Scotland. Nevertheless, he is not fit to travel or train so we have withdrawn him. He is obviously disappointed but we have to be realistic and make sure he is ready for our next match against Southampton."
